fact.en: Trap 1: Meghalaya Plateau Connection: The Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau and Karbi Anglong are NOT part of the Himalayas. They are geologically extensions of the **Peninsular Plateau**, separated from it by the Malda Fault (Garo-Rajmahal Gap).
fact.hi: Trap 1: Meghalaya Plateau Connection: The Meghalaya (Shillong) Plateau and Karbi Anglong are NOT part of the Himalayas. They are geologically extensions of the **Peninsular Plateau**, separated from it by the Malda Fault (Garo-Rajmahal Gap).

fact.en: Trap 2: Western vs Eastern Ghats Continuity: A common trap is assuming both Ghats are continuous. The **Western Ghats are continuous** and can be crossed only through passes, while the **Eastern Ghats are highly dissected, discontinuous**, and broken by major east-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri).
fact.hi: Trap 2: Western vs Eastern Ghats Continuity: A common trap is assuming both Ghats are continuous. The **Western Ghats are continuous** and can be crossed only through passes, while the **Eastern Ghats are highly dissected, discontinuous**, and broken by major east-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri).

fact.en: Trap 3: Bhabar vs Terai Characteristics: Bhabar is a dry, porous belt of gravels where streams disappear. Terai is a wet, swampy, marshy forest belt just south of Bhabar where streams re-emerge. Confusing these two is a classic UPSC trap.

fact.en: Trap 4: Island Origins: Lakshadweep islands are of **coral origin** (built up by polyps), whereas the Andaman and Nicobar islands are of **tectonic/volcanic origin** (submarine tertiary mountain ranges rising from the ocean floor).
